title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Summary

This page centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes. The intent is to provide a single reference for common operational procedures including access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. Teams should follow the workflows below; deviations require owner_team sign-off and must be recorded in the related_pages list.

Scope and ownership

- Scope: Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors acting on Redwood systems and data.
- Policy owner: People Ops (primary) and Security (secondary) for access and data controls.
- Review cadence: Annual review by People Ops and Security; ad-hoc updates for regulatory change.

1) Access & permissions

Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable approvals.

Key principles:
- Role-based permissions: Use predefined role templates (Engineering-Read, Engineering-Write, Eng-SRE, Finance-Read, Exec) mapped to groups in the identity provider (IdP).
- Approval chain: Manager approval + team owner + security review for elevated access (production, financial systems).
- Time-limited access: Elevated or emergency access must include an expiration and post-access attestation.

Standard process (requesting access):
1. Employee/contractor opens an Access Request using the Access Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-template.
2. Manager approves in the IdP (Okta/GitHub SSO ticket).
3. Team owner verifies necessity; Security performs risk checks for production/PII access.
4. Access is provisioned by the platform owner and logged.

Offboarding checklist (required steps):
- Revoke IdP account and SSO sessions
- Remove from team groups and Google Workspace groups
- Revoke cloud console keys and rotate service accounts the user owned
- Run access audit report and attach to the offboarding ticket

Access table (roles and typical permissions):

| Role | Typical systems | Permissions | Approval required |
|------|-----------------|-------------|------------------|
| Engineering-Read | GitHub, monitoring, docs | Read-only | Manager |
| Engineering-Write | CI/CD, repos | Push/deploy | Manager + Team owner |
| Eng-SRE | Prod console, runbooks | Admin on runtime services | Manager + Team owner + Security |
| Finance-Read | Billing, reporting | Read-only financial data | Finance manager |
| Exec | All necessary dashboards | Broad visibility | People Ops |

2) Change management

Purpose: Reduce risk from operational changes and provide roll-backable, auditable procedures for infra, runtime, and product changes.

Change types:
- Standard change: Low-risk routine changes documented in a ticket and approved by the team owner. (e.g., documentation updates, small config tweaks)
- Significant change: Requires change advisory board (CAB) review, test plan, and scheduled maintenance window. (e.g., schema migrations, infra upgrades)
- Emergency change: Performed to restore service; must be documented and post-mortem completed within 72 hours.

Change request procedure:
1. Create a change ticket in JIRA with type, scope, risk assessment, rollback plan, and owner.
2. For significant changes, submit to weekly CAB (email cab@redwood for agenda).
3. Schedule during approved maintenance windows and notify stakeholders 72 hours in advance.
4. Execute, validate, and close ticket with the execution notes and monitoring dashboard links.

Rollback and validation checklist:
- Ground-truth test plan (pre/post checks)
- Monitoring playbook run (latency, error rate, saturations)
- Rollback steps documented and rehearsed in a staging runbook

3) Data management

Purpose: Ensure responsible handling of company and customer data including classification, storage, access, retention, and deletion.

Data classification categories:
- Public: No restrictions.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data.
- Restricted: Customer PII, financial records, or other regulated data.

Storage and handling rules:
- Restricted data must be stored in approved encrypted stores (KMS-backed): AWS KMS/HSM, GCP KMS.
- No customer PII in ephemeral logs or third-party analytics without explicit contract-level approval.
- Data retention: follow the Data Retention Matrix (see /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).

Data lifecycle procedure (creation to deletion):
1. Classify data at creation time and record classification in the schema or dataset metadata.
2. Ensure encryption-in-transit and at-rest for Restricted datasets.
3. Apply access controls (least-privilege and time-bound access) for datasets containing Restricted data.
4. Schedule deletion or archival according to retention policy and log the deletion event.

Data breach response highlights:
- Report to Security within 1 hour of detection.
- Triage, contain, and preserve logs.
- Notify Legal and People Ops; follow the Incident Response Security playbook.

4) Procurement & expenses

Purpose: Standardize purchasing, budgeting, and travel-related expense reimbursement.

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- Purchases <= $2,000: Team lead approval.
- Purchases between $2,000 and $25,000: Dept head + Finance approval.
- Purchases > $25,000: Finance + legal + Exec sponsor.

Procurement process (summary):
1. Create a Purchase Request form (PR) in Confluence using the procurement template.
2. Attach vendor quote(s) and business justification.
3. Finance routes for budget check and issues PO when approved.
4. For SaaS/vendor contracts, include security questionnaire and vendor risk assessment before PO.

Expense reimbursement process:
- Employees submit expenses within 30 days via the company expense system with receipts attached.
- Per-diem and travel allowances follow the Travel section below.
- Finance performs monthly spot audits; fraudulent claims escalate to People Ops.

5) Vendor management

Purpose: Ensure proper vetting and ongoing oversight of vendors that process company or customer data.

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: Complete vendor intake form and initial risk classification.
2. Security & legal review: High-risk vendors require SOC2/ISO reports, penetration test summaries, and contract clauses for data handling and breach notification.
3. Contracting and SLA: Establish SLAs, escalation contacts, and audit rights.
4. Ongoing monitoring: Annual review, security attestation, and usage/Spend review.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Low: Marketing tools, non-sensitive SaaS. Controls: Contract + annual review.
- Medium: Productivity tools with company data. Controls: Contract, security questionnaire, periodic review.
- High: Systems processing Restricted data. Controls: SOC2/ISO evidence, contractual indemnities, quarterly reviews.

6) Travel policies

Purpose: Clarify allowable travel, approvals, safety, and reimbursement processes.

Pre-approval and booking:
- All business travel requires a Travel Request form and manager approval before booking.
- Use company travel vendor (Concur/tripbook) for flights and hotels; exceptions require Finance sign-off.

Allowable expenses and limits:
- Flights: Economy for domestic; Premium Economy for flights >8 hours. Exceptions need Exec approval.
- Hotels: Mid-tier business hotels; avoid per-diem rates above policy thresholds.
- Meals: Itemize and submit receipts. Alcohol reimbursed only for client entertainment with approval.

Safety and emergency procedures:
- Register travel in the company travel tracker for international trips.
- Emergency contact: Travel safety team (security@redwood.example).
- Evacuation or country risk: Follow Travel Advisory in /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-advisories.

7) Internal templates and examples

This section provides canonical templates and links. Teams should copy these templates and link their instance back to this canonical page when used.

- Access Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-template
- Change Request template (JIRA): Template: "Change Request - Standard/Significant" in JIRA library
- Purchase Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-purchase-request-template
- Vendor intake form: /confluence/policies-and-process/vendor-intake-form
- Travel Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-request-template

Governance and escalation

- Exceptions: Any exception to these policies must be submitted as an Exception Request with owner_team endorsement and retained for audit.
- Disputes: People Ops will mediate policy disputes; unresolved items can escalate to the Exec sponsor.

Appendix: Quick checklists

Onboarding new hire (people-ops checklist):
- Create HR profile and issue offer letter
- Provision IdP account (Okta) and 2FA enrollment
- Add to team groups and grant baseline access
- Complete security training within first 7 days

Significant change pre-launch checklist:
- Completed CAB review and approvals
- Runbook updated + rollback validated
- Monitoring alerts configured and tested
- Stakeholder communications drafted

Contacts and ownership

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.example (owner for policy maintenance)
- Security: security@redwood.example (data & access controls)
- Finance: finance@redwood.example (procurement & expense)
